$schema_note: AUTHORED, and it is a READING of a raster. It carries what Captain Whistler's draught of 25 January 1808 draws of the FIRST Fort Dearborn, the one burned on 16 August 1812. Boxes are hand-read in sheet pixels off the Gutenberg working copy (1600 x 2290 px, +x right, +y down) to about +/-5 px. Feet are COMPUTED from them by tools/read_whistler_1808.py, never typed, and `--check` refuses a feet figure the pixels do not give. It authors NO fabric: T-2049 builds from it and T-2050 seats it.

sheet.orientation: As printed. Lake Michigan is lettered down the right-hand margin and the river runs round the top, so the sheet's right is taken as EAST. That is INFERRED: no north arrow was found on the reproduction, so the fort's bearing to true north is NOT read here and is T-2050's question.

scale.stated: 'The measurement of the Garrison including the Block Houses And Barrick are laid down at twenty feet to the Inch' (the index's note). The inch is not recoverable from a reproduction whose reduction is not stated.
scale.measured_from: the flagstaff, lettered '75 feete' along its length. It is drawn LAID DOWN, from its foot at the centre of the parade northward through the north range, so its drawn length is its height at the garrison scale.
scale.note: One anchor, and the drafter's own. tools/read_whistler_1808.py --remeasure finds the staff's ends on the fetched sheet: a near-continuous dark run in columns 994-1007, which tolerates gaps of up to 12 px where the faint line crosses the north range's ink. It reproduces these numbers. Every feet figure below inherits this scale's error; read to +/-5 px, a box edge is good to about +/-1.1 ft.

frame: Fort feet, with the ORIGIN AT THE STAFF'S FOOT: e_ft is positive to the sheet's right (inferred east) and n_ft positive to the sheet's top. Only the garrison is in this frame. The sheet's other houses are drawn 'without any Regular rule' and carry sheet pixels only.

parade.note: The thin rectangle the barracks face. Quaife: 'in the center of which stood a lofty flagstaff'.

parts.label: north-west blockhouse
parts.drawn: plan
parts.note: The plan with its crenellated outline, numeral '1' inside. A gabled elevation is folded out to the west (x 692-748), and is not part of the box. It straddles the angle of BOTH picket rows (5 and 6 below), which is what Quaife describes: 'the blockhouses commanded not only the space without the four walls, but also that inclosed between the two rows of palisades'.

parts.label: south-east blockhouse
parts.drawn: plan
parts.note: The same drawing at the opposite angle, numeral '1' inside, with its elevation folded out to the east (x 1270-1312). Within two feet of the north-west one on both sides.

index.name: Port Holes for Cannon
index.why: No numeral '2' was read on the reproduction. The blockhouse plans carry a notched outline, but at this resolution it cannot be told whether the notches are cannon ports (2), loopholes (3) or the ends of the upper storey's logs. Quaife: one blockhouse held two small cannon, the other one.

index.name: Loop Holes for small arms
index.why: As 2.

parts.label: magazine
parts.drawn: elevation
parts.note: Drawn in ELEVATION ONLY: an arched front between two piers, numeral '4' beneath it, with its base line at y 752. So the box is its width and its place, NOT a footprint, and the depth is not on the sheet. Quaife: 'a small structure made of brick', between the north range and the north-west blockhouse. That is where it stands here.

index.name: Inward Row of pickets
index.note: Each curtain is drawn as a hatched band between the buildings, and this reading takes the band's PARADE-SIDE edge as the inward row. Every range's back wall stands on that same line (north range y 688, west x 800, east x 1205, south y 1100), so the barracks are set into the inner row rather than standing free of it. The inner row encloses x 800-1205, y 688-1100.

index.name: Outward Row of pickets
index.note: The band's OUTER edge. The band is 38-46 px wide (8.4-10.2 ft), and on the west curtain it is visibly two hatched columns of about 18 px each, divided by a line at x 780. So an alternative reading is that each column is one row of pickets drawn laid down, with no gap between them. The register takes the band's edges as the two rows because that is the arrangement Quaife describes: an enemy scaling the first row 'would only find himself within a narrow inclosure between that and the second'. T-2049 inherits the choice and must say which it builds.

parts.label: main gate passage
parts.drawn: plan
parts.note: The gap in the middle of the south range, numeral '7' at its head, between the two halves of the soldiers' barracks. A gate elevation is folded out to the south to y 1215 and is not in the box. Quaife: 'The main gateway of the stockade was at the middle of the south side and was flanked on either side by the main barracks for the common soldiers'.

index.name: Wicket Gate
index.why: No numeral '8' was read. Quaife puts it 'near the northwestern blockhouse', and the west curtain beside that blockhouse carries marks that are illegible at this resolution. They are not read as the gate.

parts.note: Plan, numeral '11' twice, elevation folded out west (x 740-800), roof beyond it to x 712. Quaife: 'directly opposite were those for the subordinate officers'.

index.name: Agents House
index.why: Inside a paled yard south-west of the fort. The Indian Department's dwellings are drawn at forty feet to the inch and their distances are 'not laid down by a scale', so only the arrangement is read. The drafter's distance line from it reads 'Distance to Main Gate Eighteen Perches' (297 ft). The sheet puts it about 91 ft from the gate at the garrison scale, so the line is not to scale, as he says.

index.name: Factors House
index.why: No numeral '18' read. A second paled house stands north of 17, at about (590, 1095), with no legible numeral. Quaife says the factor's and the agent's 'two log houses' stood 'a short distance to the southwest', so it is the CANDIDATE. It is not asserted.

index.name: Interpreters House
index.why: Numeral '19' beside it, west-south-west of the fort, the one house on the sheet drawn turned (about 32 degrees). Its distance line reads 'Distance to the Main Gate is fortyeight Perches' (792 ft), against about 115 ft on the sheet at the garrison scale, a ratio of 6.9 where 17's is 3.3. The two ratios disagree, which confirms the red-ink distances are not drawn to scale. BUILT at T-2507 by no. 17's figure, not its own: outside_the_stockade.expansions.interpreter_19 says why.

index.why: READ AT T-2507: the numeral '20' is lettered beside the front of the house south-east of the officers' garden toward the beach, after a word or two not read. Built by the outside_the_stockade rule (part armourers_shop).

index.name: Merchants Shop
index.why: READ AT T-2507 at 8x, turned to the lettering: the mark west of the small house east-south-east of the officers' garden, which T-2048 could not read at 3x, is '21'. Built by the outside_the_stockade rule (part merchants_shop).

index.name: Bake House
index.why: READ AT T-2507 at 8x, turned to the lettering: '22' beside the small building between the agent's house (17) and its distance line. Built by the outside_the_stockade rule (part bake_house).

index.name: House in Factors Dept.

index.name: Stables
index.why: READ AT T-2507 at 8x: '24' is lettered beside the north and the south buildings of the column of three south of no. 17, and '23' beside the middle one. Two stables are built (first_fort_outer_stable_north, _south).

index.name: River Cheykago
index.why: Drawn as the double line arcing round the fort's north and east. The note says 'The River is not regularly surveyed', so its course is not read for position. The 1812 shore is data/terrain's business (T-1242), not this sheet's.

index.name: Banks of said River
index.why: Drawn with 25; not read for position, for the same reason.

index.name: Wharf of said River
index.why: READ AT T-2507 at 8x: '27' between two short dotted lines that leave the river's east line west of the fort, near the north-west blockhouse and the red '122 feet to River', and meet about 24 px out: a small dotted outline standing out from the bank. The river is 'not regularly surveyed', so the mark is not read for position. BUILT AT T-2508 (first_fort_wharf), seated on the committed 1812 river by `seat` below rather than by the outside rule.

seat.rule: The drafter's own figure, on the drafter's own side. The red '122 feet to River' (unnumbered, beside this mark) is the one distance the sheet gives from the garrison to the river at the wharf. A circle of that radius about the outer picket row's north-west corner (its record's footprint, not a sheet pixel) is swept clockwise from due west, the side of the angle the sheet draws no. 27 on, and the wharf's bank foot is where it first meets the committed 1812 water (data/terrain/epochs/e1830_natural/river.geojson). The deck is laid along the bank there: the bank's line is the water's edge cast north at two points 8 m apart about the foot, the deck is centred on the foot, ties `heel_m` back into the bank and stands out `reach_px` at the outside buildings' forty feet to the inch, and its top is the committed ground at the heel's centre, as the 1835 wharves' decks take theirs (data/wharves/river_landings.json form.freeboard_m).
seat.along_bank_why: The shortest crib the pier_crib archetype builds. The sheet draws the mark about 23 px along the line, about 10 ft at forty feet to the inch; the archetype's floor governs and the difference is a liberty.
seat.heel_why: data/wharves/river_landings.json form.heel_in_m, the 1835 wharves' figure, so the deck meets ground rather than ending on the waterline.
seat.reach_why: The dotted outline stands about 24 px out from the river's line. Read at the index's forty feet to the inch for the outside buildings, that is 10.6 ft (3.24 m) beyond the committed waterline.
seat.agreement: The circle meets the water at bearing 288.4, 18 degrees north of the sheet's westward line, so the drafter's distance and his side both land on the committed bank within a turn of the page. Quaife's 'eighty feet' from the north-west corner (after Wilson) is the nearest water, due north, which the committed bank puts at 21.1 m (69 ft) from the corner. The two figures measure different lines and do not disagree.

index.name: Low ground between said bank & River
index.why: No numeral '28' read with confidence.

index.name: Beach between Sd. River and Lake
index.why: Numeral '29' on the strip between the river and 'Lake Michigan', which is lettered on the right of the sheet.

index.name: John Kinzie Esq. House on the opisite side River
index.why: Numeral '30' under the long house across the river, north-north-east of the fort, inside a fenced yard lettered as Mr Kinzie's kitchen garden.

index.name: Oather Dwelling Houses on opisite side River
index.why: Three houses across the river, each with a '31'. Quaife: 'Whistler's diagram represents three houses to the westward of Kinzie's establishment, but omits the names of their owners'. T-2504 reads their boxes in north_bank, which seats them west of the Kinzie house as built: the westernmost and the middle one built as Le Mai's and La Lime's, the eastern one left to T-2486 as Ouilmette's.

index.name: Old Grist Mill Worked by Horses
index.why: The building carrying the numeral '32' is drawn between the easternmost no. 31 house and Mr Kinzie's kitchen garden, at about sheet px [1177, 427, 1215, 455], its '32' under it near (1190, 460): found at T-2504 and recorded in T-2485. T-2485 seats it in north_bank as kinzie_horse_mill_1812; that run could not fetch the sheet to re-read it, so the box is T-2504's reading.

index.name: Covered Way to procure Water
index.why: The index: '{ N. 33 Covered Way to procure Water } Omited in their places'. It is not on the sheet. Quaife (text only): 'From the northeast corner of the stockade a covered way led to the river'. BUILT AT T-2508 (first_fort_covered_way_*), INFERRED from that text and never traced, by `seat` below.

seat.rule: Quaife p. 165: 'From the northeast corner of the stockade a covered way led to the river, securing thus to the garrison access in safety to the water in time of attack.' The passage leaves the outer picket row's north-east corner (its record's footprint) along the frame's north, its east row continuing the east curtain's line, and runs to the committed 1812 water, which is about 26.3 m off on that line. 'In safety' is read as screened, so it is built as a passage between two picket rows of the outer row's own pickets, open to the sky. It is cut into RUNS because a structure stands on the lowest ground under it: across the terrace one run, and down the 3.4 m bank three steps, each falling no more than `max_fall_m`, so the uphill end of every step still shows more than two metres of picket. Each run is its own enclosure with a gateway at both ends, `joint_m` after the one before it (the outer row's own picket spacing, so no picket of one run stands inside another's).
seat.runs_note: Metres north of the outer row's north face, along the passage's centre. The terrace run stops where the committed ground first falls off the 3.6 m terrace; the last run stops on the committed water's edge.
seat.width_why: Reconstructed: the narrowest enclosure the palisade archetype builds with a 1.5 m gateway at each end (it refuses a gate wider than half its side). No source gives the passage's width.
seat.wells: The sheet letters 'wells' (unnumbered) just outside this same angle, between the stockade and the river: the drafter's water was here. No well is built from the word.

index.name: Gutters to carry off the Water
index.why: Omitted, as 33. Quaife: 'The parade ground was surrounded by gutters for carrying off the water'.

unnumbered.label: flagstaff
unnumbered.note: The scale anchor above. Its foot is the frame's origin.

unnumbered.label: 'wells'
unnumbered.note: Lettered outside the north-east angle, between the stockade and the river. It carries no index number. No well is asserted from a word without a mark.

unnumbered.label: Comm'g Officers Garden
unnumbered.note: Eight beds in two rows south of the fort, lettered with its own scale. That scale is not read here, and the garden is placed by arrangement only. Quaife: melons and other small fruit and vegetables.

unnumbered.label: a Sutlers garden
unnumbered.note: Small fenced plot east of the officers' garden, toward the beach. Arrangement only. Quaife mentions 'a smaller garden and an Indian graveyard' between the fort and the river mouth. No graveyard is read from this sheet, and none is to be modelled from it: the depiction of Indigenous burial is the owner's question (AGENTS.md), not a reading's.

unnumbered.label: '122 feet to River'
unnumbered.note: A red-ink distance from the west side near the north-west blockhouse. On the sheet the river is about 93 px off, which is about 21 ft at the garrison scale. The figure is measured, not drawn, as the note says. Wilson/Cooper's '80 feet' from the north-west corner (Quaife p. 164) is the same kind of figure. Neither is a scale check.

cross_checks.check: the staff's foot is the parade's centre
cross_checks.detail: foot (1000, 894) against the parade box's centre (998, 890): 2 px and 4 px, under one foot. The laid-down reading of the staff is what puts its foot there.
north-west 17.3 x 19.0 ft, south-east 19.2 x 18.4 ft: the same work drawn twice, within 2 ft on both sides.

cross_checks.check: the inner row encloses a square
cross_checks.detail: x 800-1205, y 688-1100: 89.6 x 91.2 ft, square within 2 percent. Quaife: 'a quadrangle'. The outer row (x 762-1250, y 642-1145) is 108.0 x 111.3 ft.

cross_checks.check: the folded elevations agree on a two-storey height
cross_checks.detail: Each range's elevation is folded out over the curtain, and their depths disagree: south 50 px (11.1 ft), west 60 px (13.3 ft), north 70 px (15.5 ft), east 85 px (18.8 ft). Four buildings the note calls equally 'two storeys high' differ by 70 percent, so the elevations are NOT drawn at the plan scale and no height is read from them. Heights for T-2049 are a separate question, and an inferred one.

At twenty feet to the inch, 4.52 px/ft is 90.4 px to the original inch, so the 1600 x 2290 px reproduction stands for a sheet about 17.7 x 25.3 in. That is a plausible size for a manuscript draught, but no source reached states the original's size, so this is not a check.

cross_checks.check: the first fort is not the second
cross_checks.detail: The 1816 stockade is derived at about 174 ft square (data/structures/fort_dearborn_palisade.json, off Harrison 1830); this one's outer row is about 108 x 111 ft. Both blockhouses here are at the north-west and south-east angles, where the second fort had one at the south-west. Nothing of either is to be borrowed for the other (data/exclusions.json, fort_dearborn_first_1803).

for_t2049: What may be BUILT from this, and at what grade: the inner and outer picket lines, the two blockhouse footprints, the four ranges' footprints and their rooms, the main gate's place, the two small houses, the parade and the staff's place and height. All are INFERRED (a measured reading of a tier-1 sheet whose scale rests on one anchor), never documented. NOT on the sheet: heights (the elevations disagree), the wicket gate, the guard house, the stores 14 and 15, the covered way and the gutters, and the bearing to true north.

outside_the_stockade.what_this_is: The reading T-2062 adds for the buildings and gardens the draught draws OUTSIDE the stockade, and the rule they are built to. The index puts these off the garrison scale: the Indian Department's dwellings are 'laid down at forty feet to the Inch' and their distances 'not laid down by a scale'. So no part here is a measurement of where it stood. Each one is the sheet's ARRANGEMENT, opened out by a figure the drafter wrote himself. Every number below is a pixel box on the pinned sheet (sha256 above) or a figure lettered on it. tools/read_whistler_1808.py --check re-derives every record built from this from those boxes.
outside_the_stockade.the_rule: Each part is placed by its sheet offset from the main gate's outer mouth (gate_px), multiplied by an EXPANSION. A part with a stated distance or a stated scale uses its own: the agent's house (no. 17) has 'Distance to Main Gate Eighteen Perches' (297 ft), and the Commanding Officer's garden is lettered '5o feete to the Inch' (50/20 = 2.5). A part with neither uses the expansion of the nearest part that has one: the factory and the stables take no. 17's, and the sutler's garden takes the officers' garden's. A building's footprint is its drawn box at the scale the index states for the Indian Department's dwellings (40 ft to the inch), and a garden's is its drawn box at the garden's own lettered scale. The drawn buildings are small pictorial elevations, roof and front together, so a footprint read this way is an upper bound and is RECONSTRUCTED. The positions are reconstructed too. T-2507 adds nos. 19-22 under the same rule. 'Nearest' is the nearest part with its own figure, centre to centre on the sheet, among the parts T-2062 read: the bake house (22) beside no. 17 takes no. 17's; the armourer's shop (20) and the merchant's shop (21), east and south-east of the officers' garden, take the garden's, as the sutler's garden does. The interpreter's house (19) states its own distance, and that figure is KEPT BUT DOES NOT GOVERN (expansions.interpreter_19 says why): it takes no. 17's. A building drawn turned off the sheet's axes carries turn_deg, its box is its plan in its own axes about its drawn centre, and it is seated turned by that angle.
outside_the_stockade.inch_px_note: One inch of the garrison scale: 20 ft at the staff's 4.52 px per foot. The other two scales are fractions of the same inch.
outside_the_stockade.gate_px_note: The main gate passage's south mouth: index no. 7's box [950, 1100, 978, 1150], mid-width at its outer edge. The drafter's distance lines end 'to Main Gate'.

agent_17.stated: Distance to Main Gate Eighteen Perches
agent_17.note: A perch is 16.5 ft. The sheet puts the house's centre about 89 ft from the gate at the garrison scale, so the drafter's figure is about 3.3 times the drawing.

garden_scale.stated: Comm'g Officers Garden 5o feete to the Inch
garden_scale.note: READ AT T-2062, on a 4x crop of the lettering above the garden's north side. The first figure is the period 5 with a looped head, so it is easily taken for an 's'; 'so feete' makes no sense and '5o' does. The 2048 register left this scale unread. It is inferred and not attested.

interpreter_19.stated: Distance to the Main Gate is fortyeight Perches
interpreter_19.note: READ, KEPT AND NOT USED (T-2507). A perch is 16.5 ft. The sheet puts the interpreter's house's centre about 115 ft from the gate at the garrison scale, so this figure is about 6.9 times the drawing where no. 17's is 3.3. Under the rule's own priority (a part with a stated distance uses its own) it would seat no. 19 with one corner of its footprint 0.4 m inside the committed 1812 river (data/terrain/epochs/e1830_natural/river.geojson) and its centre 4.5 m from the edge. A house cannot stand in the river, so ONE of the two is wrong, and the river governs: it is drawn from Wright's 1834 survey, while the drafter says outright that his outside distances are 'not laid down by a scale' and his two figures already disagree by a factor of two. No. 19 therefore takes no. 17's expansion like every other building west of the fort, which keeps the sheet's arrangement among them, the one thing it does draw. Possible reasons the figure runs long (a distance walked by the road, which bends here, rather than a straight line) are not asserted. tools/read_whistler_1808.py --check refuses this expansion if any part uses it, and refuses any outside record with a footprint corner on the 1812 water.

parts.drawn: pictorial elevation, roof to the west and a two-storey front of six lights to the east, with a paled yard lettered 'Paling' east of it
parts.identity: The paled house north of no. 17, at the head of the column of buildings west of the fort, with no numeral read (index no. 18 stays not_located). It is BUILT as the factory, and the identification is inferred from two statements that agree. Quaife says the factor's and the agent's 'two log houses' stood 'a short distance to the southwest'. The Chicago Magazine of March 1857, on chicagology_prefire052, puts 'the two-story log United States factory west of the fort', and this is the one house of the pair that stands due west.

parts.drawn: pictorial elevation drawn like the factory, numeral '17' beside it, its paled yard east of it with the distance line running from it

Its front faces east like the column below it; where the others draw a pitched roof to the west it draws a hatched, ROUNDED shape. That may be an oven's dome or a roof drawn round, and is read as neither: the record carries a gable. A smaller mark just south of it, about [561, 1255, 580, 1272], has no numeral and is not built.

the third of the three

a small ruled plot east of the officers' garden toward the beach, lettered 'a Sutlers Garden', with one small house inside it. The house is not built: its numeral is not legible, and the register's no. 21 reading of a mark near it stays unread.

READ AT T-2507 on a 5x crop. A pictorial elevation drawn TURNED about 32 degrees anticlockwise off the sheet's axes, the only house on the sheet drawn so: its front, with two rows of two lights, runs from about (425, 1283) up to (493, 1240) and faces south-south-east (bearing 148), the roof drawn behind it to the north-north-west. sheet_px is the plan in the drawing's own axes about its centre (451, 1242.5): 80 px along the front, 47 px deep; drawn_bbox_px is the turned drawing's extent on the sheet. The numeral '19' is the register's reading.

READ AT T-2507 on 5-6x crops. The house south-east of the officers' garden toward the beach: a front of lights facing west with its roof, and a lower piece on it, drawn to the east. Lettered beside its front, reading down the sheet, a word or two and the numeral '20'; the numeral is clear, the words before it are not read (they may name the trade, and are not asserted).

READ AT T-2507 at 8x, turned to its lettering. The small house east-south-east of the officers' garden that the register found with an illegible mark: the mark, west of its front, reads '21'. A front with two lights facing west, its roof drawn to the east.

outside_the_stockade.not_built: The paled yards beside nos. 17 and 18, and the 'Old field' lettered west of the road, which is ground rather than a structure. The small unnumbered mark south of the bake house (no. 22). The house inside the sutler's garden, whose mark is not read. The wharf (no. 27) and the covered way (no. 33) are T-2508's: they are seated on the river rather than by this rule. Until T-2507 the interpreter's house (no. 19) was here too; it is now built, by no. 17's expansion (expansions.interpreter_19).

north_bank.what_this_is: The reading T-2504 adds for the three houses the draught draws across the river WEST of Kinzie's, each with a '31' (index no. 31, 'Oather Dwelling Houses on opisite side River'), and the rule they are seated by. Boxes are read off the pinned sheet at T-2504, on 4x crops with 10 px ticks; they are the drawn house, roof and front together, chimney left out, and good to about +/-3 px. They supersede no. 31's centres in the index, which were read at T-2048 as the place of each numeral and its house together.
north_bank.the_rule: T-2062's outside rule (outside_the_stockade.the_rule) with ONE CHANGE OF ORIGIN. That rule opens the sheet out about the main gate. Applied here it would seat the Kinzie house (no. 30) at fort-frame E +272 ft, N +415 ft, about 80 m east of where kinzie_house_1812 stands by its texts ('directly facing the fort', on the flagstaff's easting: T-2497), and it would put two of the three no. 31 houses EAST of the built Kinzie house when the sheet draws all three west of it. So the north bank is opened out about the Kinzie house AS BUILT: each part is its sheet offset from no. 30's drawn box centre, times the expansion, added to kinzie_house_1812's footprint centre in the fort frame. That keeps the one thing the sheet does draw on this bank, the houses' order and spacing along it, and hangs it on the one house there that the sources place. A footprint is the drawn box at the index's forty feet to the inch, as for every outside building, so it is an upper bound and RECONSTRUCTED; so is every position. A part drawn turned off the sheet's axes carries turn_deg as in outside_the_stockade. A part whose record is null is read and not built here: its ticket is named. T-2513 adds Coursoll's worm-fenced field west of the houses: a field is ground and carries no lettered scale, so its drawn outline is opened out by the bank's expansion (scale_ft_per_in 'expansion'), as the gardens' outlines outside the stockade are by theirs.

anchor.note: No. 30's main block, roof and front, without the lean-to drawn against its east end (to x 1422). The record is the main house only (12.2 x 6.7 m), so the anchor is its centre.

expansion.note: READ AT T-2504, lettered above the picket fence the sheet draws along the north bank from the westernmost no. 31 to the middle one; under it, 'Picket of 5 feet high', and a line too faint to read whole. A yard is 3 ft. The line runs from the fence's west corner, where the paling up the side of the inclosed field meets it, to the middle house's west wall. It is the ONE figure the drafter wrote on this bank, and it measures the very interval between two of the houses, so under T-2062's own priority (a part with neither figure takes the NEAREST part that has one) it governs here rather than no. 17's eighteen perches, which is a distance on the other side of the fort. No. 17's expansion would open the bank about a third wider (agent_17 is kept, below) and set the westernmost house 74 m from the middle one against the fence's 47.5 m. The paling up the field's east side carries a length too ('... yards in length'); its figure was not read with confidence and is not used.

kept.agent_17: outside_the_stockade.expansions.agent_17, the ticket's first reading (T-2504's 'the same frame and expansion as the agent's house'). Computed by --check for comparison and never used: it contradicts the fence's lettered length by the margin the expansion note gives.

parts.drawn: a log house, its front of lights to the river, a chimney on its west gable; drawn tilted with the bank, its eave rising 14 degrees to the east, at the south-east corner of the worm-fenced field lettered 'Mr Coursell' and the west end of the 52-yard picket
the largest of the three: a log house, front of three lights and a door to the river, a chimney on its east gable, the 52-yard picket ending at its west wall
the smallest: a log house, one light and a door, a chimney on its west gable, between the middle house and the building numbered 32 beside Kinzie's garden
parts.occupant: Ouilmette, inferred: the one no. 31 house nearest Kinzie's, where Currey's 'close in the rear of the Kinzie house' and Wau-Bun's 'close at hand' put his. Built by T-2486.
parts.read: Re-read at T-2486 on a 12x gridded crop of the pinned sheet: the chimney stands on the west gable (x 1124-1132), the door left of the middle (x 1132-1135, y 460-469) and the one light right of it (x 1142-1147, y 461-467), so their centres stand 0.345 and 0.607 of the box from its west end.

parts.occupant: Coursoll, attested: 'a house and inclosed field north of the river, belonging to Mr. "Coursoll."' (Quaife 1913 p. 167); the sheet letters 'Mr Coursell' inside it.
parts.drawn: READ AT T-2513 on 3x and 6x crops. West of the three no. 31 houses: a field bounded by a zigzag lettered 'Worm Fence' along its south-west side, 'Mr Coursell' inside it, drawn TURNED about 29.5 degrees anticlockwise off the sheet's axes. Its corners read about N (707, 387), W (522, 490) and S (611, 604). Three sides are the zigzag. The fourth, from N down to the bank at about (748, 525), is the hatched paling whose length T-2504 could not read; the westernmost no. 31 house (no31_west) stands across the field's south-east corner, the south-east zigzag ending at its west gable. The corners make a skewed quadrilateral, so the field is read as a box in its own axes: 184 px along it (the mean of its two long sides), and across it from the north-west side down to the south-east side as far as the house allows (108 px of the drawn 141), because the house stands OUTSIDE the fence at that corner and a box carried to the drawn south-east side would put the fence through it. sheet_px is that box about its own centre; drawn_bbox_px is the turned drawing's whole extent.
parts.scale_note: No scale is lettered at the field and it is not a building, so the index's forty feet to the inch does not apply. A field is ground: its outline is a set of distances on the ground like the ones between the houses, so it is opened out by the bank's own expansion (the '52 yards in length' on the picket), as the gardens outside the stockade are by theirs.

parts.drawn: a small building with a pitched roof between the easternmost no. 31 house and Mr Kinzie's kitchen garden, its numeral '32' under it; index no. 32, 'Old Grist Mill Worked by Horses'
parts.read: Box read at T-2504 and recorded in the T-2485 ticket ('Found at T-2504'); not re-read at T-2485, whose container could not fetch the sheet. Faces the river as the draught draws the houses on this bank (reconstructed).
